[Doc 1] Rostker v. Goldberg: Rostker v. Goldberg, 453 U.S. 57 (1981) , was a decision of the United States Supreme Court holding that the practice of requiring only men to register for the draft was constitutional.

[Doc 2] Rostker v. Goldberg:  (The named defendant is Bernard D. Rostker, Director of the Selective Service System.)

[Doc 3] Rostker v. Goldberg:  After extensive hearings, floor debate and committee sessions on the matter, the United States Congress enacted the law, as it had previously been, to apply to men only.

[Doc 4] Rostker v. Goldberg:  Several attorneys, including Robert L. Goldberg, subsequently challenged the gender distinction as unconstitutional.

[Doc 5] Rostker v. Goldberg:  In a 6-3 decision, the Supreme Court held that this gender distinction was not a violation of the equal protection component of the due process clause, and that the Act would stand as passed.
